pages.title: FaustBot Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to FaustBot: what it is, its architecture, key subsystems, and how the backend, frontend, and external services fit together. Links to all major child sections.

pages.title: Getting Started & Installation
pages.purpose: Step-by-step guide for setting up FaustBot: prerequisites (Node.js, Anaconda/Python), cloning the repo, installing Python and npm dependencies, configuring API keys, and launching the system for the first time.

pages.title: System Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: Describes the overall multi-process architecture: Python FastAPI backend, Electron frontend, sidecar services (TTS, ASR, RAG, MC Operator), and how they communicate via HTTP REST and WebSocket. Introduces the agent abstraction and the LangGraph reasoning loop.

pages.title: Backend Core
pages.purpose: Overview of the Python backend: FastAPI service, agent runtime lifecycle, configuration system, and the key modules in faust_backend/. Links to child pages for each major subsystem.

pages.title: Configuration System
pages.purpose: Explains the dual-file configuration strategy (faust.config.json + faust.config.private.json), the config_loader module, global variable population, CLI argument overrides, and the reload_configs() hot-reload mechanism.

pages.title: Agent Runtime & LangGraph Integration
pages.purpose: Deep dive into how the LangGraph agent is created, how SQLite checkpoints and stores persist conversation state, the agent_lock concurrency model, rate-limit retry logic, and the rebuild_runtime lifecycle.

pages.title: Agent Management & Administration
pages.purpose: Covers the admin_runtime module: listing, creating, deleting, and switching agents; the agent directory structure (AGENT.md, ROLE.md, COREMEMORY.md, TASK.md); diary and record file access; and the masked-secret configuration save pattern.

pages.title: LLM Tools & Agent Capabilities
pages.purpose: Documents all tools available to the FAUST agent: system/environment tools, file I/O and patch mode, diary management, Python/shell execution, GUI operator, Live2D motion control, Human-in-the-Loop approval, Nimble window creation, RAG query tools, and Minecraft integration tools.

pages.title: Trigger System
pages.purpose: Explains the event-driven trigger architecture: trigger types (datetime, interval, py-eval, event, nimble-reminder, nimble-expire), the trigger queue, append/fire filter chains, persistence via triggers.json, and how triggers inject messages into the agent's chat loop.

pages.title: Security & Human-in-the-Loop
pages.purpose: Describes the security verifier sub-system (SECURITY_VERIFIER_LLM), access level controls (unlimited/loose/standard/strict/disabled), path-pattern matching, and the HIL (Human-in-the-Loop) approval workflow using asyncio Futures and the /faust/humanInLoop/feedback endpoint.

pages.title: Plugin & Skill System
pages.purpose: Overview of FaustBot's extensibility architecture: the PluginManager, PluginContext protocol, ToolSpec/MiddlewareSpec interfaces, skill packages, and the plugin market. Links to child pages for plugin development and bundled plugins.

pages.title: Plugin System Internals
pages.purpose: Details the PluginManager class: plugin discovery from the plugins/ directory, manifest loading (plugin.json), hot-reload via file fingerprinting, state persistence in plugins.state.json, and the plugin lifecycle (startup, on_load, register_tools, register_middlewares, on_unload).

pages.title: Developing Plugins & Middlewares
pages.purpose: Developer guide for writing FaustBot plugins: the PluginContext API (trigger_create, get_config, set_config), ToolSpec and MiddlewareSpec registration, the mm_bridge multimodal_tool_result contract, filter_trigger_append/fire hooks, and the string-based config schema format.

pages.title: Bundled Plugins
pages.purpose: Describes the plugins shipped with FaustBot: clipboard (read/write), context_manager (context trimming middleware), search_tools (web search), ui_operator (screen OCR + automation), vision_tools (screenshot capture), and mm_bridge (multimodal message transformation).

pages.title: Plugin Market
pages.purpose: Explains the faust_plugin_market web UI and plugins.json registry: how plugins are listed, the faustbot://install_plugin deep-link protocol, the install-zip backend endpoint, conflict resolution (409 overwrite flow), and how to publish plugins to the market.

pages.title: Skill System
pages.purpose: Covers the skill_manager module: what skills are (agent-scoped tool packages in skill.d/), their _meta.json and SKILL.md structure, how they differ from plugins, installation via installOpenClawSkillTool, and management through the admin API.

pages.title: Speech & Audio Pipeline
pages.purpose: Overview of the multi-modal audio stack: TTS, ASR, and VAD subsystems, their local vs. OpenAI-compatible modes, and how they integrate with the frontend. Links to child pages for each component.

pages.title: Text-to-Speech (TTS)
pages.purpose: Details the TTS subsystem: local GPT-SoVITS mode vs. OpenAI-compatible mode, the TTS_REFER_WAV_PATH voice cloning reference, TTS_PROMPT_TEXT, the local TTS sidecar service on port 5000, the /faust/audio/tts proxy endpoint, and sequential sentence queuing for lip-sync.

pages.title: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) & Voice Activity Detection (VAD)
pages.purpose: Covers the ASR pipeline: local vs. OpenAI-compatible modes, the ASR sidecar on port 1000, energy threshold and silence detection parameters. Also covers the VAD WebSocket (/faust/audio/ws/vad), Silero VAD integration, client-side 16kHz resampling, pre-roll buffering, and the barge-in feature.

pages.title: RAG Memory System
pages.purpose: Overview of the Retrieval-Augmented Generation long-term memory system: LightRAG service, the rag_client module, document tracking, auto-indexing of chat history, and the RAG admin API. Links to child pages for client details and admin management.

pages.title: RAG Client & Document Tracker
pages.purpose: Deep dive into rag_client.py: the docTracker class (MD5-based change detection, rag_doc_tracker.json, rag_chat_history_records.json), synchronous and asynchronous RAG query patterns, the auto-index pipeline, and the nano-vectordb alternative backend.

pages.title: RAG Administration & Memory Management
pages.purpose: Covers the admin-facing RAG features: the /faust/admin/rag/documents paginated search API, document content retrieval, the RAG memory bank UI in configer_pyside6.py, agent alignment (align_rag_agent), and the RAG_AUTO_INDEX_RECORD setting.

pages.title: Frontend
pages.purpose: Overview of the Electron-based desktop frontend: the Live2D overlay window, the app.js interaction layer, the PySide6 configuration tool, and supporting UI components. Links to child pages for each major frontend area.

pages.title: Electron Main Process
pages.purpose: Covers electron-main.js: window creation (transparent, always-on-top, fullscreen enforcement), the static:// and faustbot:// custom protocol handlers, IPC handlers (set-ignore-mouse-events, focus-main-window, open-config-window), global hotkeys, the command WebSocket client, and the PySide6 configer launcher.

pages.title: Live2D Avatar & Interaction Layer (app.js)
pages.purpose: Details app.js: PIXI.Application setup, Live2D model loading and scaling, drag-and-drop with position persistence, hit testing and motion triggers, the ASR bubble chat UI, tool call cards, streamed TTS with sequential playback, lip-sync via Web Audio API RMS, and the click-through mouse penetration system.

pages.title: Nimble Interaction System
pages.purpose: Explains the Nimble (灵动交互) subsystem end-to-end: the nimble.py session manager, showNimbleWindowTool and closeNimbleWindowTool, the three-trigger lifecycle (result, reminder, expire), the window.nimble.submit() JavaScript API, the /faust/nimble/callback endpoint, and HIL_APPROVAL overlay.

pages.title: Configuration UI (PySide6 Configer)
pages.purpose: Documents configer_pyside6.py: the ConfigerWindow class, dynamic form generation from FIELD_METADATA, AI provider settings, Live2D configuration, TTS/ASR speech controls, agent lifecycle management (create/switch/delete/reset checkpoint), plugin and skill management panels, and the RAG memory bank UI.

pages.title: Minecraft Integration
pages.purpose: Overview of the AI-plays-Minecraft feature: the mc-operator Node.js WebSocket server, the Python minecraft_client.py, MC event triggering, and the agent tools for connecting and issuing in-game commands.

pages.title: MC Operator Service
pages.purpose: Details the mc-operator Node.js WebSocket server: the BotManager (mineflayer bot lifecycle), the command router (connect, chat, execute commands), the event bridge (broadcasting game events to connected clients), and the WebSocket protocol message format.

pages.title: Minecraft Agent Tools & Event Triggers
pages.purpose: Covers the Python side of Minecraft integration: minecraft_client.py WebSocket client, the minecraftConnectTool/minecraftCommandTool/minecraftStatusTool LangChain tools, MC_EVENT_TRIGGER_ENABLED configuration, and how game events flow through the trigger system into the agent's chat loop.
